new_roles.title: Director of Portfolio Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
-------------------

The Portfolio Group, under the Workplace Experience Group umbrella, delivers seamless experiences from the breakroom to the boardroom, providing a signature suite of services for each unique business portfolio. Our team builds partnerships that excel, creating experiences that break the mold, where convenience, consistency, and excellence are a given. One Partner. Infinite Solutions.

As a District Manager, you will provide overall vision, planning, direction, and control to assigned units for a large and complex geographic district normally generating $30-50M+ in revenue. This key leadership role is accountable for execution of our General Management program, with a focus on growth, cost and productivity, leading people and delivering financial commitments.

Whether focused on multiple sites for a large client or multiple clients, the key success measures of a District Manager include Revenue Growth, EBIT, Margin, Consumer Satisfaction, Client Loyalty and Employee Engagement.

In this role, frequent travel to client sites throughout the district is expected.

**Compensation Data**
---------------------

COMPENSATION: The Salaried rate for this position is $160,000.00 to $175,000.00. If both numbers are the same, that is the amount that Aramark expects to offer. This is Aramark's good faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation for this position as of the time of posting.

BENEFITS: Aramark offers comprehensive benefit programs and services for eligible employees including medical, dental, vision, and work/life resources. Additional benefits may include retirement savings plans like 401(k) and paid days off such as parental leave and disability coverage. Benefits vary by location and are subject to any legal requirements or limitations, employee eligibility status, and where the employee lives and/or works. For more information about Aramark benefits, click here Aramark Careers - Benefits & Compensation

There is no predetermined application window for this position, the position will close once a qualified candidate is selected. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all applicable laws, including, but not limited to all applicable Fair Chance Ordinances and Acts. For jobs in San Francisco, this includes the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

**Job Responsibilities**
------------------------

The successful candidate demonstrates capability across the following dimensions:

* Leadership - Establish overall ownership and accountability of operational management and financial performance of multiple accounts and units. Model key leadership behaviors and ensure the highest levels of safety, quality and service excellence for employees, clients, and consumers. Coach & mentor employees by crafting a shared understanding about how and what needs to be achieved. Reward and recognize employees. Identify and engage top talent and develop team members to their fullest potential within the organization. Plan and lead team management meetings. Ensure safety and sanitation standards in all operations.
* Client Relationship - Establish and maintain effective client and customer rapport for a mutually beneficial business relationship. Identify client needs and communicate operational progress. Understand contractual obligations and leverage opportunities. Facilitate and support new business and retention activities. Ensure team completes customer satisfaction surveys in all locations.
* Financial Performance - Build revenue and manage budget with sensitivity to costs and client needs. Ensure the completion and maintenance of P&L statements for the district. Provide oversight and take ownership to deliver client and company financial targets using Aramark systems. Understand performance metrics, data, order and inventory trends; educate teams on key levers to improve margins.
* Productivity - Lead managers in implementing and maintaining corporate management agenda for labor and financial initiatives. Ensure value through efficient operations, appropriate cost controls, and profit management. Ensure consistent application of Aramark's operating standards and processes (Operational Excellence) with particular focus on efficiency standards. Understand end to end supply chain and procurement process and systems; ensure only authorized suppliers are used.
* Compliance - Ensure unit managers maintain a safe and healthy environment for clients, customers and employees. Follow all applicable policies, rules and regulations, including but not limited to those relating to safety, health, and wage and hour.

At Aramark, developing new skills and doing what it takes to get the job done make a positive impact for our employees and for our customers. In order to meet our commitments, job duties may change or new ones may be assigned without formal notice.

**Qualifications**
------------------

In order to be prepared for this leadership role, qualified candidates will possess:

* Proven leadership experience, typically acquired over 5-10 years, including P&L responsibility within the hospitality, retail, facilities, direct store delivery or food and beverage industries.
* Demonstrated leadership skills with a broad knowledge of management practices, business judgement and client/consumer interaction.
* Confirmed ability to hire, assess, develop and grow hard-working talent.
* Comfortable reading, understanding, and implementing contractual requirements, including identifying opportunities within contract terms and conditions to address operational issues.
* Established communication and teamwork skills to work with all levels on the organization from the front line associate through leadership.
* Proven success in a repeatable business model, including leading through change and turnaround initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree is generally required to be successful; advanced degree in business or related field is preferred.

**Education**
-------------

**About Aramark**
-----------------

**Our Mission**

Rooted in service and united by our purpose, we strive to do great things for each other, our partners, our communities, and our planet.

At Aramark, we believe that every employee should enjoy equal employment opportunity and be free to participate in all aspects of the company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, pregnancy, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, military status, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by applicable law.

**About Aramark**

The people of Aramark proudly serve millions of guests every day through food and facilities in 15 countries around the world. Rooted in service and united by our purpose, we strive to do great things for each other, our partners, our communities, and our planet. We believe a career should develop your talents, fuel your passions, and empower your professional growth. So, no matter what you're pursuing - a new challenge, a sense of belonging, or just a great place to work - our focus is helping you reach your full potential. Learn more about working here at http://www.aramarkcareers.com or connect with us on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter.

Whether focused on multiple sites for a large client or multiple clients, the key success measures of a District Manager include Revenue Growth, EBIT, Margin, Consumer Satisfaction, Client Loyalty and Employee Engagement.
**Job Responsibilities**
* Leadership - Establish overall ownership and accountability of operational management and financial performance of multiple accounts and units.

identity_held_roles.title: Program Director - Quality & Customer Success (6900)
identity_held_roles.description:
As **Program Director III - Quality & Customer Success**, you'll report directly to the Executive Vice President of the Intelligence Portfolio. This role oversees quality assurance and customer success. The Program Director removes delivery impediments, strengthens collaboration across teams, ensures compliance with contract requirements, and advocates for successful customer outcomes.

We know that you can't have great technology services without amazing people. At MetroStar, we are **obsessed** withour people and have led a two-decade legacy of building the best and brightest teams. Because we know our future relies on our deep understanding and relentless focus on our people, we live by our mission: A passion for our people. Value for our customers.

If you think you can see yourself delivering our mission and pursuing our goals with us, then check out the job description below!

**What you'll do:**

* Constantly monitor project progress to identify impediments early on, actively engage in resolving them, and 
 escalate issues when necessary.
* Manage and track dependencies across cross-functional teams or squads to ensure seamless collaboration and 
 timely delivery.
* Oversee and track all high-integrity commitments, ensuring they are met according to established timelines and 
 standards.
* Provide proactive visibility into project status, communicate delivery targets, commitments, and progress 
 effectively to stakeholders.
* Define, implement, and administer program deliverables to ensure full compliance with contract requirements. 
 Regularly report progress on problem resolution to senior management, highlighting any critical issues or 
 roadblocks.
* Foster a culture of team-driven decision-making and commitment, promoting trust among team members and 
 facilitating team-building events.
* Support customer meeting preparation and delivery and assist with escalations.
* Perform any other duties as assigned by senior leadership to support the overall objectives of the organization

**What you'll need to succeed:**

 

* Active TS//SCI with ability to obtain CI poly
* Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
* 10+ years of quality assurance experience, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Proven success implementing and managing quality assurance processes and practices.
* Strong understanding of software development methodologies and quality assurance principles.
* Demonstrated ability to identify and resolve delivery impediments, manage dependencies across teams, and escalate critical issues.
* Experience overseeing program deliverables to ensure compliance with contract requirements, timelines, and quality standards.
* Ability to track commitments and clearly communicate project status, delivery targets, risks, and resolution progress to stakeholders and senior leadership.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, and collaboration skills, including supporting customer meetings and managing escalations.
* Strategic thinking and the ability to identify and prioritize improvements in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
* Ability to build trust, encourage team-driven decisions, and promote accountability across cross-functional teams.

 

SALARY RANGE: $185,000- $225,000

The salary range for this position is determined based on qualifications, skills, and relevant experience. The final salary offered will be determined based on several factors including:

* The candidate's professional background and relevant work experience
* The specific responsibilities of the role and organizational needs
* Internal equity and alignment with current team compensation
* This role is also eligible for additional compensation, subject to the terms and policies of MetroStar, which may include:
* + Performance-based bonuses
 + Company-paid training and/or certifications
 + Referral bonuses

**Application Deadline:** Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled; candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible for full consideration.

**Additional Compensation**: This role may also be eligible for bonuses and/or additional incentives based on individual and company performance.

**Benefits**: All full-time employees are eligible to participate in our benefits programs:

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) retirement plan with company match
* Paid time off (PTO) and holidays
* Parental Leave and dependent care
* Flexible work arrangements
* Professional development opportunities
* Employee assistance and wellness programs

Like we said, **we are** big fans of our people. That's why **we offer** a generous benefits package, professional growth, and valuable time to recharge. Learn more about our company culture code and benefits. Plus, check out our accolades.

**Commitment to Non-Discrimination** 
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment based on merit and without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

**What we want you to know:**

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

**Not ready to apply now?**

Sign up to join our newsletter here.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Quality & Compliance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Reports to:** Executive Director

 

**Job Summary:**

The Director of Quality and Compliance for the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) Program will oversee and manage all aspects of quality assurance, compliance, and regulatory adherence for the PACE program. This role ensures that the program operates in full compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, as well as upholds the highest standards of care for the elderly participants. The Director will lead efforts to continuously improve program quality, enhance participant satisfaction, and drive performance excellence across the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

1. Regulatory Compliance Management:

* Ensure adherence to all PACE-related federal, state, and local regulations, including CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) and state-specific requirements.

* Monitor and interpret updates to regulatory policies, and adjust organizational practices as necessary to remain compliant.

* Act as the primary liaison between the organization and regulatory agencies, ensuring timely reporting and response to audits, surveys, and inspections.

2. Quality Assurance and Improvement:

* In collaboration with the Medical Director develop, implement, and evaluate quality improvement initiatives to ensure high standards of care, safety, and service delivery for participants.

* Collaborate with clinical and operational teams to analyze performance metrics and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

* Oversee the development and execution of corrective action plans (CAPs) for any areas of deficiency, ensuring timely resolution.

3. Risk Management and Reporting:

* Lead risk assessment processes to identify potential compliance and quality issues, minimizing risk to the organization and participants.

* Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies, including monitoring trends, identifying patterns, and taking proactive actions.

* Ensure the organization is prepared for external audits and inspections, managing all compliance-related documentation and reporting.

4. Staff Training and Development:

* Develop and conduct ongoing training programs for staff on compliance, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

* Foster a culture of compliance and continuous improvement across the organization by leading educational initiatives and creating awareness.

* Provide guidance and support to staff on regulatory changes, quality standards, and best practices.

5. Participant Care and Satisfaction:

* Advocate for participants’ safety and satisfaction, ensuring that their rights and well-being are protected in all aspects of the program.

* Work closely with interdisciplinary teams to ensure person-centered care is at the core of all service delivery and interventions.

* Monitor and evaluate participant feedback, addressing any concerns or complaints in a timely and professional manner.

6. Leadership and Strategic Planning:

* Serve as a key member of the senior leadership team, contributing to the strategic direction of the PACE program.

* Collaborate with leadership to set annual goals for quality and compliance performance and develop strategies to achieve these objectives.

* Ensure alignment of quality and compliance initiatives with organizational goals and values.

7. Data Collection and Analysis:

* Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of quality and compliance data to track program performance and outcomes.

* Utilize data to drive decision-making and identify areas for operational improvements and resource allocation.

* Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership and external stakeholders regarding compliance, quality, and performance metrics.

8. Technology and EMR

* Serving as the primary point of contact for EMR-related issues, providing guidance and troubleshooting support to team members.

* Leading training sessions and providing ongoing support for staff to ensure efficient use of the EMR system.

* Collaborating with IT and management teams to implement updates and resolve system issues.

* Continuously staying updated on new features and best practices for the EMR system to ensure the organization is utilizing the platform to its full potential.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, nursing, public health, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

* Minimum of 4 years of experience in quality management, compliance, or regulatory affairs in a healthcare setting, with at least 2 years in a leadership role.

* Knowledge and experience with PACE program operations and regulations (CMS and state-level).

* Strong understanding of healthcare regulations, accreditation standards, and compliance protocols.

* Proven track record in leading quality improvement initiatives and risk management programs.

* Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.

* Ability to work collaboratively across departments and with interdisciplinary teams.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to drive results.

* Certification in Healthcare Quality (CHCQM, CPHQ) or other relevant certifications preferred.

**Physical Demands:**

* Ability to work in an office environment and attend in-person meetings.

* Occasional travel to program sites or regulatory meetings may be required.

**Work Environment:**

* A collaborative, team-oriented atmosphere within a dynamic, fast-paced healthcare environment.

* Commitment to participant-centered care and service excellence.

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
identity_held_roles.description:
**About Genesis**
=================

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

**The role**
------------

We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.

This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
* Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
* Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
* Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
* Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
* Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
* Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
* Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
* Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
* Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
* You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
* Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
* You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
* You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
* You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
* 8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
* Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.

**Why this role**
-----------------

You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.

**How we work**
---------------

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

* **Limitless ambition.** We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
* **Relentless urgency.** Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
* **Type-2 Fun.** Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
* **Radical transparency.** Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
* **Multiculturalism.** We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
* **Team over ego.** Help others, share context, and win as a team.
* **A joyful journey.** We take pride in the craft.

identity_held_roles.title: Head of Operational Excellence
identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

**Job Description**

The Head of Operational Excellence will lead operational excellence across Shield AI’s Group 3 UAV manufacturing in Frisco, TX (V-BAT) and Group 5 UAV manufacturing in Seattle, WA (X-BAT). Based in Frisco, this leader will create, deploy, and actively manage manufacturing KPIs and performance systems across both sites, embedding operating rhythms that improve accountability, visibility, and results. 
 
You will be responsible for instilling a culture of execution excellence, embedding structured problem-solving practices, and delivering measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and productivity. This includes leading the development and governance of operational standards—such as visual management, 5S, and root cause analysis—while owning the manufacturing budget cycle, business rhythm, and executive reporting interface across both locations. This role partners with engineering, production, quality, and business functions to execute high-priority improvement initiatives, support V-BAT production, and establish operational excellence as X-BAT progresses through prototype and into rate production.

**Do you have the expertise and leadership to embed excellence into the fabric of autonomous defense manufacturing?**

### **What You'll Do:**

* Create, deploy, and actively manage consistent manufacturing KPIs and performance dashboards across both sites to drive visibility and accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.

* Define, train, deploy, and continually improve operational standards across V-BAT manufacturing in Frisco and X-BAT manufacturing in Seattle, including 5S, root cause analysis, and visual management.

* Develop and institutionalize the manufacturing budget process across both sites, including forecasting, controls, and performance tracking.

* Set financial targets in collaboration with operations and finance teams and drive adherence to budget and cost goals.

* Lead high-impact cross-functional improvement initiatives across both sites to improve quality, delivery, efficiency, productivity, and cost performance.

* Prepare and coordinate senior and executive-level reporting packages for Manufacturing leadership reviews.

* Partner with production, quality, and engineering teams to deploy Lean and continuous improvement practices, adapting execution to the needs of established production and prototype-to-rate manufacturing.

* Own business office functions for Manufacturing across both sites, including goal tracking, KPI dashboards, and process governance.

* Coach and train teams and leaders across both sites to elevate operational discipline, share effective practices, and sustain improvements.

### **Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or related field.

* Experience leading operational excellence, Lean, or business office programs within a manufacturing environment, with the ability to lead improvement across multiple sites.

* Demonstrated ability to design, roll out, and sustain structured operational standards and improvement systems.

* Strong background in budgeting, reporting, and performance management at a senior level.

* Excellent communication skills and experience preparing executive-level summaries and presentations.

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree or formal Lean Six Sigma certification.

* Experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware manufacturing environments.

* Proficiency with digital tools for KPI visualization, reporting automation, and business process tracking.

* Track record of influencing change across large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and multiple sites.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality Engineering and Automation -Information technology
existing_roles.description:
Overview:

ServiceLink is seeking an experienced Director of Quality Engineering and Automation to lead our quality engineering transformation. This leader will be responsible for defining and executing the enterprise quality strategy, modernizing test automation capabilities, establishing quality governance standards, and driving engineering-wide quality improvements.

This role is not a traditional QA management position focused solely on test execution. The Director will serve as the organization’s quality engineering leader, responsible for building scalable automation capabilities, establishing meaningful quality metrics, and influencing software quality outcomes across Engineering, Product, and Release organizations.

The ideal candidate combines deep quality engineering expertise with strong organizational leadership, executive communication skills, and a proven ability to drive meaningful change in highly matrixed environments. Success in this role requires the ability to influence decisions through data, credibility, partnership, and quality leadership rather than direct organizational authority.

ServiceLink is modernizing the mortgage services industry through AI-accelerated engineering, intelligent automation, and next-generation software delivery practices. We empower the nation’s top lenders and financial institutions with advanced technology, data-driven insights, and high-velocity product development models.

As we continue to scale our technology platforms, we are investing in a modern Quality Engineering organization focused on automation, quality governance, engineering excellence, and continuous delivery. Our goal is to transform quality from a downstream testing activity into an engineering capability embedded throughout the software development lifecycle.

**This is a hybrid role, and will be required to work in-office at our Plano, TX office at least 3 days per week. Candidates must be located within reasonable commuting distance of this office and be willing to work in-office on a regular basis.**

**Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require sponsorship for employment visa status now or in the future.**

A DAY IN THE LIFE

In this role, you will…

* Lead quality engineering transformation
* Own enterprise test automation strategy
* Establish quality governance and risk management policies and procedures
* Drive engineering quality excellence
* Influence cross-functional release and product outcomes
* Establish quality metrics and executive reporting
* Lead and develop the Quality Engineering organization

Success Measures

* Automated coverage of critical business workflows.
* Reduction in manual regression testing effort.
* Improved release predictability and confidence.
* Reduction in escaped production defects.
* Increased adoption of shift-left quality practices.
* Expanded developer ownership of quality.
* Enhanced visibility into quality trends and release readiness risks.
* Increased executive confidence in quality governance and software delivery outcomes.

WHO YOU ARE

You possess …

* 10+ years of progressive experience in software quality, quality engineering, software engineering, or related technology leadership roles.
* 5+ years of experience leading quality engineering organizations in complex enterprise software environments.
* Demonstrated success leading large-scale test automation and quality transformation initiatives.
* Experience building and scaling automation frameworks and engineering quality practices.
* Strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and cloud-native application architectures.
* Experience implementing API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
* Experience establishing quality metrics, executive scorecards, and data-driven governance models.
* Strong understanding of risk management, release readiness, and quality governance practices.
* Experience managing distributed teams and complex organizational change efforts.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and business audiences.
* Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering and testing tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies.

Responsibilities:

1. Lead Quality Engineering Transformation

* Define and execute a multi-year quality engineering strategy aligned with ServiceLink’s technology and business objectives.
* Transform the organization from a predominantly manual testing model to an automation-first quality engineering approach.
* Establish scalable operating models, standards, and best practices across quality engineering functions.
* Evaluate and implement AI-assisted testing capabilities where they provide measurable business value.
* Continuously improve testing effectiveness, release confidence, and overall software quality.
* Develop a strategic roadmap that reduces manual regression testing effort while improving coverage and reliability.

2. Own Enterprise Test Automation Strategy

* Define and execute automation strategies spanning unit, API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing.
* Build and maintain modern automation frameworks supporting multiple product portfolios and technology stacks.
* Identify opportunities to automate repetitive testing activities and reduce release-cycle effort.
* Establish automation standards, coding practices, and framework governance.
* Drive automation adoption across engineering teams and development pipelines.
* Ensure automation investments directly support business outcomes through measurable reductions in manual testing effort

and improved release quality.

3. Establish Quality Governance and Risk Management

* Define enterprise quality standards, testing policies, and release readiness criteria.
* Develop risk-based testing frameworks that focus resources on the highest-value business scenarios.
* Provide objective assessments of release readiness and software quality risks.
* Establish processes for identifying, documenting, communicating, and escalating quality concerns.
* Lead post-release reviews and quality retrospectives to identify systemic improvement opportunities.
* Create clear mechanisms for risk visibility and executive decision support.

4. Drive Engineering Quality Excellence

* Partner with software engineering leaders to embed quality throughout the SDLC.
* Champion shift-left testing practices and developer ownership of quality.
* Promote increased use of automated testing within CI/CD pipelines.
* Drive adoption of engineering practices that improve code quality, testability, maintainability, and system reliability.
* Collaborate with architecture and development teams to improve overall product quality and reduce defect introduction

rates.

* Influence engineering decisions through quality metrics, technical insights, and continuous improvement recommendations.

5. Influence Cross-Functional Release and Product Outcomes

* Build strong working relationships across Product Management, Release Management, Engineering, Operations, and

Support organizations.

**Organization Overview:**

Sound Community Services, Inc. (SCSI) is a private, not-for-profit organization dedicated to educating, assisting, and supporting individuals with persistent mental illness and substance use disorders. We work tirelessly to create a culture and environment in which recovery and wellness are possible.

**Position Overview:**

The Director of Quality Assurance (QA) oversees all agency activities related to quality improvement, compliance, data integrity, and regulatory preparedness for the agency. This position provides leadership in the development, implementation, and monitoring of systems that support clinical excellence, consumer rights, performance measurement, and regulatory compliance. The Director plays a critical role in the maintenance, configuration, and optimization of the Electronic Health Record (EHR); oversees required state reporting; maintains the centralized repository of all Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) reported data; and ensures accurate and timely data submission. This role also leads the agency’s preparation for external audits (ex., Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF), Department of Public Health (DPH), DMHAS), coordinates customer satisfaction activities, and serves as the agency’s Client Rights Officer.

This position is responsible for the monitoring and analyzing of processes to meet Fidelity and contractual requirements across the agency. Ongoing analysis of health care information obtained from a variety of sources, including patient care, financial, and demographic data is necessary. This role involves the development and preparation of information for state reporting and organizational best practices. This position will maintain repository of all state reported data for all DMHAS programs. A heavy importance is placed on collaborating with program leaders across the agency, ensuring accuracy of data reported and driving agency performance.

* Train employees and monitor compliance across programs with state reporting requirements.
* Function as an internal information expert to the entire management team when special and critical quality issues occur.
* Consult with senior leadership to resolve quality, service, and efficiency problems.

**State Reporting, Data, and Surveys**

* Provide DMHAS Data Performance System (DDaP) data and informational support to other departments, including DDaP 101 supervisor training, share DMHAS information with leadership, and present quarterly and annual DMHAS Report Cards to leadership.

**Electronic Health Record (EHR) and Systems Support**

* Facilitate within the EHR the build and support of procedures, forms, and form development; implement training to identified employees.
* Foster ongoing support to assigned programs and serve as a liaison between staff and vendors for effective responses to users’ needs.

**Audit Readiness, Compliance, and Quality Improvement**

* Provide support to programs in preparation for routine external audits, including CARF survey, fidelity reviews, and Department of Public Health licensing.
* Facilitate completion of all corrective action plans and audit follow-up, including quarterly and annual program compliance reviews.
* Monitor and assist with corrections and work with programs to identify and resolve root causes as needed.
* Ensure compliance with SCSI’s policies, quality assurance programs, and safety; ensure EHR compliance with regulatory agencies like DMHAS, DPH, CARF, etc.
* Participate in quality improvement initiatives.

**Agency Participation and Policy Compliance**

* Participate in all agency activities pertaining to health and safety, training, drills, etc.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly.

existing_roles.description:
ElevateBio is a technology-driven company powering the industry forward by helping partners realize the potential of their therapies from design to commercialization. We have integrated a differentiated set of technologies, end-to-end services, and industry-leading manufacturing expertise to develop advanced therapies faster and more efficiently.

  

**The Role**

The Senior Director, Quality Control leads all Quality Control operations at ElevateBio's Waltham site, including QC Analytical Technologies (QCAT), QC Analytics, Testing Core, QC Microbiology, QC Raw Materials, and QC Logistics. The role is accountable for safe, compliant, inspection-ready, and predictable execution across a seven-day operating model, including product release and in-process testing, STAT support to Manufacturing, environmental and microbiological testing, raw material disposition, stability support, sample management, and analytical lifecycle enablement. The Senior Director establishes the QC operating strategy, capacity and resource plan, performance system, and leadership model required to meet manufacturing, client, and business commitments while sustaining laboratory excellence and data integrity.

**Here's What You'll Do**

**QC Strategy and Leadership**

* Lead the integrated QC organization, operating model, objectives, decision rights, talent strategy, and capability roadmap.
* Develop QC management and technical leaders while aligning headcount, seven-day coverage, facilities, equipment, systems, operating expense, and capital with demand.

**Predictable QC Operations and Laboratory Excellence**

* Own safe, compliant, and predictable execution of product release and in-process testing, environmental and microbiological monitoring, raw material disposition, stability, sample management, and client commitments.
* Ensure reliable seven-day operations through capacity planning, schedule control, tiered daily management, performance review, and timely escalation and recovery.
* Partner with Manufacturing to align readiness, prioritization, and rapid execution of STAT in-process samples within required decision windows.
* Drive laboratory excellence through standard work, right-first-time execution, efficient review and reporting, backlog control, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.

**Analytical Technologies and Lifecycle Enablement**

* Provide leadership oversight for QCAT, including client technical interface, technology and method transfer, qualification and validation, method lifecycle management, equipment qualification, controls and critical reagents, and Digital QC.
* Ensure effective utilization of shared QC Resources, handoffs between QCAT and operational laboratories through clear readiness criteria, accountability, sustainable capacity, and post-implementation monitoring.

**Quality, Compliance, and Partnership**

* Ensure QC activities meet cGMP, approved procedures, specifications, quality agreements, data-integrity expectations, and regulatory commitments.
* Provide senior oversight of laboratory events, atypical or out-of-specification results, deviations, investigations, CAPAs, changes, risks, and inspection readiness.
* Represent QC in client governance, audits, regulatory inspections, release-readiness reviews, and escalations; communicate performance, constraints, risks, and recovery plans clearly.
* Serve as the senior QC partner to Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Facilities & Engineering, MSAT, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, Digital, Process and Analytical Development, and site leadership.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Biology, Microbiology, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline; an advanced degree is preferred.
* At least 15 years of progressive experience in GMP Quality Control or analytical laboratory operations, including substantial leadership of managers and multi-functional teams.
* Demonstrated leadership of a broad QC organization supporting complex biopharmaceutical, biologics, cell therapy, gene therapy, or other regulated manufacturing operations.
* Strong knowledge of GMP laboratory controls, analytical testing, microbiology, environmental monitoring, raw materials, stability, sample management, analytical lifecycle activities, laboratory systems, data integrity, contract laboratory oversight, and quality systems.
* Demonstrated success improving schedule reliability, turnaround time, right-first-time performance, capacity utilization, investigation management, and inspection readiness.
* Experience leading seven-day operations and partnering with Manufacturing on time-critical in-process testing and operational decision windows.
* Experience supporting client audits, regulatory inspections, client governance, and significant quality or delivery escalations.
* Strong strategic planning, financial stewardship, organizational design, talent development, communication, decision-making, and stakeholder-management capabilities.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean Six Sigma, Lean Lab, and Digital Lab practices to improve laboratory flow, capacity, data visibility, and operational performance is preferred.
* Experience in a multi-program or CDMO environment is preferred.

**Physical and Environment Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, bend and stretch for extended period of time
* Ability to lift 15-20 lbs
* Ability to push, pull, bend, kneel, twist and climb step ladders while wearing PPE.
* Ability to perform routine repetitive motions with use of arms, wrists and hands

**Lead Strategy. Drive Performance. Shape the Future.**

KSP Group, Inc/Jensen Metal Products is seeking a hands-on manufacturing leader to drive operational excellence, strengthen accountability, improve execution, and build scalable operating systems across our manufacturing businesses. This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.

We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.

This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.

**About KSP Group**

KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies

* **Jensen Metal Products** – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
* **Jensen Powder Finishers** – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)
* **Jensen Castings** – Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI)
* **Real Flame** – A leading designer and manufacturer of fireplaces, fire tables, and outdoor living products sold through major retailers across North America (Union Grove, WI)

Together, our companies are built on innovation, craftsmanship, customer partnerships, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.

**What You'll Do**

Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

* Lead the development and execution of operational strategies that support long-term business objectives and growth initiatives
* Partner with executive leadership to establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive enterprise-wide operational improvements
* Lead plant leadership teams in defining strategic direction, performance goals, and key operational initiatives
* Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
* Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
* Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
* Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
* Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
* Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results

Leadership & Culture

* Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
* Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment

Requirements:

**What We're Looking For**

* Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:
* Production planning and scheduling
* Labor performance management
* Quality improvement initiatives
* Corrective action processes
* Maintenance and equipment planning
* Capital investment justification
* Safety and operational accountability
* Frontline leadership development
* Proven track record of transforming entrepreneurial manufacturing organizations into process-driven, scalable operations through both strategic leadership and active engagement with frontline teams
* Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy
* Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, machining, finishing, assembly, materials management, and manufacturing cost drivers

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or related field, preferred
* Multi-site manufacturing leadership experience
* Lean Six Sigma certification
* Experience within both contract manufacturing and consumer products environments
* ERP/MRP system experience

**Travel Requirements**

* Regular travel between KSP Group facilities, including Jensen Metal Products, Jensen Powder Finishers, Jensen Castings, and Real Flame locations
* Frequent presence on manufacturing floors to support leadership teams, operational reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Approximately 25-50% travel, primarily within Wisconsin and company operating locations
* Occasional overnight travel for customer visits, supplier meetings, strategic initiatives, and industry events

**About Us**

Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. We serve many types of businesses including the agricultural, retail, energy and healthcare fields. From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. At Jensen Metal Products we pride ourselves on having strong, long-lasting relationships with our employees and customers. We welcome you to join our team!

* Competitive base salary plus profit sharing
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options (HDHP and copay), FSA benefits, and the ability to use your existing HSA
* Company-funded medical deductible reimbursement — up to $1,000 (individual) / $2,000 (family)
* 401(k) with company match up to 4%
* Life and disability insurance and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Paid time off and company holidays

* A collaborative, team-oriented environment with direct access to leadership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing organization
* Company-sponsored team events and outings that foster connection and celebrate team success

**Work Authorization**

Jensen Metal Products does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Recruiting Agencies**

Jensen Metal Products does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies, recruiting firms, or search agencies. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to Jensen Metal Products employees or through our application process will become the property of Jensen Metal Products, and no fee will be paid if the candidate is hired.

existing_roles.description:
**About Loenbro**

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

**At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose.** Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps expand the reach of the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

  

**Job Summary**

The Director of Quality - Fabrication & Manufacturing is responsible for developing, implementing, and leading the enterprise quality strategy across Loenbro's Fabrication & Manufacturing network. This position will establish a consistent, scalable quality management framework supporting mechanical and pipe fabrication, structural fabrication, electrical prefab, modular assembly, and future manufactured products across Loenbro facilities.

A primary initial responsibility will be conducting a comprehensive assessment of existing facility certifications, code qualifications, quality programs, procedures, personnel qualifications, inspection capabilities, and customer-specific requirements. The Director will use this assessment to establish a fleet-wide certification and quality strategy aligned with Loenbro's target markets, facility specialization, and long-term manufacturing strategy.

The Director will lead the transition from predominantly project-specific quality control toward a proactive manufacturing quality model centered on first-time quality, error prevention, standardized processes, measurable performance, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement. The role will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Project Management, Welding and Process Improvement, Safety, Estimating, Supply Chain, Business Development, project teams, and customers to ensure consistent quality delivery.

The Director will also develop quality plans and strategies supporting new products, manufacturing processes, facilities, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and expansion into new end markets, while serving as a senior customer-facing quality leader capable of confidently articulating Loenbro's quality systems, capabilities, certifications, controls, and continuous-improvement philosophy.

  

**Essential Job Responsibilities**

**Enterprise Quality Strategy & Governance**

* Develop and implement a standardized Fabrication & Manufacturing quality strategy across Loenbro's manufacturing network.
* Establish enterprise quality standards, policies, procedures, governance, and minimum requirements across mechanical, structural, electrical prefab, modular assembly, and manufactured-product operations.
* Transition the organization toward a prevention-based manufacturing quality model focused on building quality into the process rather than relying primarily on final inspection.
* Define quality roles, responsibilities, accountability, escalation processes, and standardized expectations across facilities and projects.
* Develop a scalable quality framework capable of supporting Loenbro's growth from project-based fabrication into repeatable manufacturing.

**Certification & Qualification Strategy**

* Conduct a comprehensive assessment and gap analysis of existing certifications, accreditations, code stamps, welding qualifications, procedures, inspection capabilities, personnel qualifications, and facility-specific quality programs.
* Develop and maintain a centralized certification and qualification matrix across all Fabrication & Manufacturing facilities.
* Establish a fleet-wide certification strategy defining which certifications and qualifications should be maintained, expanded, consolidated, or added at individual facilities.
* Align certification investments with facility specialization, customer requirements, target markets, and Loenbro's hub-and-spoke manufacturing strategy.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable AWS, ASME, AISC, NEC/NFPA, UL, ISO, customer-specific, and other relevant requirements as applicable to Loenbro's work.
* Establish governance for welder qualifications, welding procedures, inspection personnel qualifications, calibration programs, and required quality records.
* Develop the quality-system roadmap required to support increasingly regulated and technically demanding markets, including future nuclear/NQA-1 capability where aligned with Loenbro's strategy.

**First-Time Quality & KPI Management**

* Develop and maintain a standardized Fabrication & Manufacturing quality scorecard focused on first-time quality, error prevention, trend visibility, and accountability.
* Track weld reject and repair rates, weld first-pass acceptance, NDE rejection rates, rework hours and cost, scrap, dimensional and fit-up nonconformances, drawing/fabrication errors, NCRs, corrective-action closure and recurrence, customer issues, supplier quality, punch-list deficiencies, electrical prefab defects, testing failures, first-pass yield, cost of poor quality, and quality-related schedule impacts.
* Establish leading indicators in addition to traditional lagging quality metrics.
* Create dashboards that provide leadership visibility into performance by facility, project, product, process, welder, supplier, and other relevant dimensions.
* Benchmark facilities and processes to identify best practices, systemic risks, and improvement opportunities.

**Mechanical, Welding & Structural Quality**

* Partner closely with Welding and Process Improvement leadership to establish consistent welding quality standards across the fabrication network.
* Monitor weld reject rates, repair rates, NDE performance, welder performance, WPS adherence, consumable controls, and recurring defect trends.
* Ensure appropriate welding procedures, qualifications, documentation, inspection requirements, material traceability, dimensional control, coatings, and testing requirements are maintained.
* Establish quality controls for structural fabrication, skids, racks, modular assemblies, equipment integration, and related manufactured products.
* Identify systemic fabrication and welding issues and implement corrective and preventive actions across affected facilities.

**Electrical Prefab Quality**

* Partner with Electrical Prefab leadership to establish appropriate quality controls for electrical assemblies and manufactured products.
* Develop standardized inspection, testing, documentation, traceability, and acceptance requirements appropriate to the type and complexity of electrical prefab being produced.
* Establish metrics addressing assembly errors, wiring and termination defects, dimensional issues, testing failures, labeling/documentation deficiencies, and field rework attributable to prefab.
* Support standardized work instructions, inspection points, testing protocols, and product acceptance criteria as electrical prefab evolves toward increasingly standardized and productized solutions.

**Quality Planning & New Product Introduction**

* Develop quality plans for major projects, new products, new manufacturing processes, and new end markets.
* Participate early in productization and design-development activities so quality requirements are incorporated into product and manufacturing-process design.
* Establish inspection and test plans, hold/witness points, acceptance criteria, documentation requirements, traceability, and turnover packages as appropriate.
* Participate in design reviews, constructability reviews, manufacturing-readiness reviews, and new-product introduction processes.
* Identify potential failure modes before production and establish controls designed to prevent defects, using risk-based methods such as FMEA where appropriate.
* Establish first-article, prototype, pilot-production, and production-release processes for new standardized products.

**Corrective Action & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish a consistent NCR, root-cause analysis, corrective-action, and preventive-action process across the manufacturing network.
* Ensure significant quality events are investigated to determine systemic causes rather than simply correcting individual defects.
* Track corrective actions through implementation and verify effectiveness to prevent recurrence.
* Identify recurring trends across facilities and deploy enterprise-level corrective actions where appropriate.
* Partner with Operations and Process Improvement to reduce variation, eliminate recurring defects, improve productivity, and lower the cost of poor quality.
* Establish mechanisms for sharing lessons learned and best practices across the network.

**Project, Customer & Commercial Quality**

* Partner with project teams early to understand project-specific quality requirements and translate them into executable shop quality plans.
* Ensure alignment among engineering requirements, procurement specifications, fabrication processes, inspection, testing, documentation, and turnover.
* Serve as a senior escalation point for significant Fabrication & Manufacturing quality matters.
* Participate in customer quality meetings, audits, facility assessments, pre-award qualifications, and strategic pursuits.
* Clearly and confidently articulate Loenbro's fabrication and manufacturing quality systems, certifications, capabilities, controls, and performance to customers.
* Support Business Development and Estimating with quality strategies and requirements for strategic pursuits and new end markets.

**Supplier Quality**

* Partner with Supply Chain to establish supplier and subcontractor quality requirements for critical materials, equipment, components, and outsourced fabrication.
* Develop risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, performance-management, and corrective-action processes.
* Track supplier-related NCRs, defects, documentation issues, and other quality impacts and ensure requirements flow through purchase orders and subcontracts.

**Quality Systems, Documentation & Digitalization**

* Standardize quality documentation, inspection records, turnover packages, NCR processes, audit records, certification records, and records-retention requirements across facilities.
* Partner with Operations and IT to evaluate and implement digital quality-management capabilities supporting the F&M network.
* Develop reliable data collection and analytics that integrate quality information with manufacturing, ERP/MRP, project controls, and operational reporting systems.
* Ensure quality records and traceability requirements scale appropriately as Loenbro moves toward repeatable manufacturing.

**Facility Strategy, Acquisitions & Integration**

* Assess quality systems, certifications, personnel, procedures, and capabilities of potential acquisition targets.
* Identify certification gaps, compliance risks, required investments, and integration requirements during acquisition due diligence.
* Develop quality integration plans for acquired facilities and support facility specialization decisions.
* Participate in new facility planning to ensure appropriate quality infrastructure is incorporated from the beginning.

**Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Provide functional leadership to quality personnel supporting Fabrication & Manufacturing facilities and projects.
* Establish competency requirements, training standards, and development pathways for quality professionals.
* Build a culture where quality is owned by Operations and the workforce, with Quality serving as system owner, technical resource, verifier, and improvement partner.
* Promote transparency, accountability, stop-work authority, learning, standardized work, and proactive error prevention.

  

**Key Performance Indicators**

* Weld reject and repair rates, and weld first-pass acceptance.
* NDE rejection rates and inspection performance.
* Rework hours and cost, scrap, and cost of poor quality.
* Dimensional and fit-up nonconformances, and drawing/fabrication errors.
* NCR volume, corrective-action closure, and recurrence rates.
* Customer issues, punch-list deficiencies, and supplier quality performance.
* Electrical prefab defects and testing failures.
* First-pass yield and quality-related schedule impacts.

  

**Strategic Priorities**

* Baseline all existing F&M certifications, qualifications, procedures, and quality capabilities.
* Develop a fleet-wide certification and qualification roadmap aligned with target markets and facility specialization.
* Establish common quality standards and governance across the manufacturing network.
* Implement a standardized F&M quality scorecard and first-time-quality metrics.
* Reduce welding defects, rework, recurring NCRs, and overall cost of poor quality.
* Establish consistent corrective-action, lessons-learned, and error-prevention processes.
* Integrate quality planning into engineering, productization, estimating, and project execution earlier in the lifecycle.
* Develop scalable quality systems for standardized mechanical, electrical, structural, skid, modular, and integrated M&E products.
* Strengthen customer-facing quality capabilities to support external F&M growth.
* Establish the quality foundation necessary to pursue more sophisticated and regulated markets, including future NQA-1 nuclear capability.

  

**Key Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive quality leadership experience in fabrication, manufacturing, construction, EPC, industrial services, or related environments.
* Demonstrated experience developing and implementing quality-management systems across multiple facilities or operating locations strongly preferred.
* Strong knowledge of welding and fabrication quality systems, inspection, NDE, material control, traceability, and corrective-action processes.
* Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, AISC, ISO, and other relevant fabrication/manufacturing requirements.
* Experience supporting electrical manufacturing or prefab quality programs preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with root-cause analysis, corrective/preventive action, first-pass yield, cost of poor quality, and continuous improvement.
* Experience developing project-specific and product-specific quality plans and supporting customer audits and qualification activities.
* Experience with new-product introduction, acquisition due diligence, and integration preferred.
* Experience with nuclear quality systems or NQA-1 is highly desirable as Loenbro develops future nuclear manufacturing capabilities.
* Strong analytical and executive communication skills, with the ability to convert quality data into actionable operational improvements.
* Ability to travel regularly among Loenbro fabrication and manufacturing facilities and project locations.

  

**Leadership Competencies**

* **Enterprise Mindset** — Thinks beyond individual shops and establishes systems that improve performance across the entire manufacturing network.
* **Quality Leadership** — Builds a culture where quality is designed into the work and owned throughout the organization.
* **Technical Credibility** — Engages confidently with craft professionals, inspectors, engineers, project leaders, executives, and customers.
* **Prevention Focus** — Prioritizes error prevention and process control over inspection and correction after the fact.
* **Data-Driven Decision Making** — Uses meaningful KPIs and trend analysis to identify risks and improvement opportunities.
* **Root-Cause Discipline** — Drives corrective actions that address systemic causes and prevent recurrence.
* **Customer Confidence** — Clearly articulates Loenbro's quality capabilities and strategy to sophisticated customers.
* **Continuous Improvement** — Develops scalable solutions that improve quality, productivity, and predictability.
* **Cross-Functional Leadership** — Collaborates effectively across Operations, Engineering, Welding, Project Management, Supply Chain, Estimating, Business Development, Safety, and project teams.
* **Builder Mentality** — Establishes systems, standards, processes, and organizational capabilities required for a growing manufacturing enterprise.

  

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Construction Management, Manufacturing, Welding Engineering/Technology, or a related technical discipline preferred; equivalent significant relevant experience may be considered.

  

**Measures of Success**

Initial success will be demonstrated through completion of a comprehensive network-wide certification and quality-capability assessment; establishment of a clearly defined fleet certification strategy; implementation of standardized quality KPIs and first-time-quality reporting; measurable reduction in weld rejects, rework, recurring NCRs, and cost of poor quality; and implementation of consistent quality planning and corrective-action processes across Fabrication & Manufacturing.

Longer-term success will be measured by Loenbro's ability to deliver increasingly complex and repeatable fabricated and manufactured products with predictable first-time quality, maintain the certifications and quality systems required by targeted end markets, demonstrate continuous quality improvement across the manufacturing network, and establish a scalable quality platform supporting Loenbro's transformation from project-based fabrication into a differentiated manufacturing business.

  

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Work Environment:**

* Primarily based in a manufacturing/fabrication shop and office environment, with regular travel across Loenbro's Fabrication & Manufacturing facilities and project sites.
* Frequent visits to fabrication shops, manufacturing floors, and industrial job sites to assess quality programs, certifications, and inspection capabilities.
* Potential exposure to noise, dust, welding fumes, and other typical industrial and manufacturing environment factors while touring facilities.
* Regular engagement with customers, auditors, and facility personnel, which may require regional and national travel by air and ground transportation.

*This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.*

  

**Benefits**

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) retirement plan with company match
* Performance-based bonus plan
* Long-term Incentives
* Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay
* Life and disability insurance
* Professional development and training opportunities
* Employee assistance program (EAP)

*Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.*

  

Guided by **Core Values (LEAD)**, grounded in **grit** and a **commitment to excellence**, Loenbro **betters** our families, customers, and **local** communities. If you're ready to be part of a company that **LEADS** by:

* **L****iving with Integrity**
* **E****xceeding Expectations**
* **A****cting with Urgency**
* **D****elivering Excellence**

…we want to hear from you.

The company is committed to eliminating preventable treatment errors and enhancing patient, clinician and environmental safety. B. Braun Medical is headquartered in Bethlehem, Pa., and is part of the B. Braun Group of Companies in the U.S., which includes B. Braun Interventional Systems, Aesculap® and CAPS®.

Braun Medical, visit www.bbraunusa.com

Ready to lead where science, quality, and patient safety come together? Join B. Braun and shape the future of laboratory excellence while driving the strategy, compliance, and innovation behind critical healthcare products.

**Why this role matters:**

The Director, Lab Quality Control serves as the senior site authority for Quality Control Chemistry and Microbiology, providing the scientific and operational leadership needed to protect product quality and maintain regulatory compliance. This role establishes the site’s laboratory strategy, leads critical quality initiatives, and ensures that laboratory operations remain scientifically sound, inspection-ready, and aligned with business and product portfolio requirements.

**How you will make an impact:**

* Develop, maintain, and execute the site Quality Control strategy in alignment with business objectives, product portfolio requirements, and regulatory expectations.
* Provide strategic oversight for QC Chemistry and QC Microbiology operations, including release, stability, raw material, in-process, microbiological, and sterility-related testing activities.
* Establish and govern laboratory standards for testing compliance, data integrity, investigations, sample management, analytical methods, specifications, and laboratory workflows.
* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.
* Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Sterility Assurance, Engineering, Validation, Technical Services, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs to support site operations and timely product release.
* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

**What sets you up for success:**
